module_title: Derived Units, Practical Units of Distance, and Scalars vs. Vectors
introduction: At this level, we memorize the units formed by combining basic units and explore the extreme scales of physics—from the massive distances of galaxies to the microscopic sizes of atoms.

core_concepts.title: Important Derived Units
core_concepts.description:
1. Force -> Newton (N) or $kg \cdot m/s^2$ 
2. Work / Energy / Heat -> Joule (J) or $N \cdot m$ 
3. Power -> Watt (W) or $J/s$ 
4. Pressure -> Pascal (Pa) or $N/m^2$ 
5. Frequency -> Hertz (Hz) or $s^{-1}$.

core_concepts.title: Astronomical Units of Distance
core_concepts.description:
1. Astronomical Unit (AU): The average distance between the Earth and the Sun ($1.5 \times 10^{11}$ m). 
2. Light Year (ly): Distance light travels in one year. 
3. Parsec: The LARGEST practical unit of distance used in astronomy. ($1 \text{ Parsec} = 3.26 \text{ Light Years}$).

core_concepts.title: Microscopic Units of Length
core_concepts.description:
1. Micron (μm): \(10^{-6}\) meters. 
2. Nanometer (nm): \(10^{-9}\) meters. 
3. Angstrom (Å): \(10^{-10}\) meters (used for measuring the wavelength of light). 
4. Fermi (fm): \(10^{-15}\) meters (used for measuring the size of an atomic nucleus).

core_concepts.title: Scalars vs. Vectors
core_concepts.description:
1. Scalar: Quantities that have ONLY magnitude (size) and no direction. (e.g., Mass, Speed, Distance, Work, Energy, Time). 
2. Vector: Quantities that have BOTH magnitude and a specific direction. (e.g., Velocity, Displacement, Force, Acceleration, Momentum).

important_entities.name: Electric Current
important_entities.significance: Electric current flows in a specific direction through a wire, but it is STILL classified as a 'Scalar' quantity. This is because it does not follow the vector laws of addition (triangle/parallelogram laws).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Force is a vector, and Displacement is a vector. But when you multiply them (Dot Product) to get Work, the result is a SCALAR. Work and Energy have no direction.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Vectors often involve 'movement with purpose' or 'push/pull'
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Displacement (moving to a specific point), Velocity (speed in a direction), Force (pushing in a direction), Acceleration (speeding up in a direction).

exam_strategy_tips:
'Which of the following is the largest unit of length?' -> Always choose Parsec. 
'What is the unit to measure the size of a nucleus?' -> Always choose Fermi.
